solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Directed towards back street to get unusual kind of medicine

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the little word for 'directed towards' end to end

parts.note: directed towards something is directed on it, giving ON
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: Someone is sent down a back street to buy an unusual medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, a patent medicine of doubtful worth.

clue.text: Starting to develop a hint of nastiness prior to ascent

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter of nastiness is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something nasty begins to show just before a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something nascent is just coming into being, beginning to grow.

clue.text: Sanction changes to cover husband's means of support

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around and so cover the husband's letter
the letters of the word sanction are changed into a new order

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An official sanction is altered to protect a husband's financial support.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar that holds up a structure, a physical support.

clue.text: Drive back from dance without Penny

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the dance sits outside the penny

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Someone is driven home from a dance with no money in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, so P goes into REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to repel an attack is to force the attackers to retreat.

clue.text: Transfix my French setter with an increase in sound

parts.note: mes is French for my (with a plural noun)
the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: in sound means the word for an increase is spelt the way it is said

parts.note: a rise is an increase, as in pay

explanation.surface: An instruction to dazzle my French crossword setter by turning up the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: RISE said aloud gives RIZE, with the Z of the -ize spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mesmerize is to hold someone spellbound, as if hypnotised.

clue.text: Game, unfinished one, about to keep John playing

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the jumbled name inside them
about means the shortened word is turned the other way round
unfinished means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: one stands for the game just named, so it means the word game

indicators.note: playing suggests the name's letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A game is left unfinished while someone waits for John to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' points back to 'Game': GAME 'unfinished' is GAM, which 'about' turns into MAG; this holds HJON, the letters of JOHN rearranged by 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahjong is a Chinese game for four players, played with tiles.

clue.text: Damp from fine spray carrying over

indicators.note: the spray carries, so holds, the letter for over

parts.note: mist is a fine spray of droplets
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Things get damp from fine spray drifting over them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something moist is slightly wet.

clue.text: Point out frivolous noble earlier

indicators.note: earlier tells us the noble word goes in front of the frivolous one

parts.note: high can mean noble or lofty, as in high-minded
light can mean frivolous, as in light entertainment

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a lightweight aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to highlight something is to draw attention to it.

clue.text: Additional concern after losing opener

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, which is lost here

parts.note: bother is trouble or concern

explanation.surface: One more worry crops up after an opening batsman is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' sounds like cricket but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: other can mean further or extra, as in 'one other thing'.

clue.text: Clear off with contract unable to be found

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it
something that cannot be found is lost

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave holds a contract that has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'get lost!' is a rude command to go away.

clue.text: Small instrument for cutting

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A small tool used for cutting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sharp blade or a sharp remark is cutting.

clue.text: Photo capturing Heather with South American catapult

indicators.note: the photo word captures, so encloses, the plant and the compass point

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A photo shows a woman called Heather with a South American weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase but splits: South gives S, American goes with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slingshot is the US word for the forked toy a British child calls a catapult.

clue.text: Extremely good for former partner to find a girl in Connecticut

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut
Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man is delighted that his ex has found a girlfriend in Connecticut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: excellent means outstanding, of the very highest quality.

clue.text: Instruction for players from City — "Try accepting a bit of responsibility"

indicators.note: the city and the try word together accept, so take in, the small piece

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the crossword's favourite city
to have a go is to try

indicators.note: a bit of means only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A city team's manager urges players to show some responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a tempo marking telling musicians to play slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Heard gossip on the way back implicating earl

indicators.note: implicating means folding in, so the earl's letter goes inside
on the way back means the gossip word is read in reverse

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: A rumour about an earl was overheard on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns DIRT into TRID, and E goes inside that. 'Heard' is about a court, not listening.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that is heard in court is tried there; both mean examined by a judge.

clue.text: Why speaking with Maria did wrong by old farm worker

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put into an incorrect order
speaking means the word why is taken as it is said, a single letter

parts.note: the word why sounds like the letter Y
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks Maria why she wronged an old farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, the sound of 'why', is mixed in with MARIA DID; 'wrong' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid was a woman employed to milk cows and make butter on a farm.

clue.text: Taunt in pub gets social worker justifiably angry

indicators.note: in places the taunt word inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a dig is a jibe or taunt
an ant is a social insect; a worker ant is a social worker

explanation.surface: A social worker is taunted in a pub and is rightly furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is the crossword's ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant describes anger at unfair treatment, so the anger feels justified.

clue.text: Put off by spot of grease on hospital department cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off

indicators.note: a spot of means a small amount, here the first letter

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A hospital department's cleaner is put off by a grease stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent, like washing powder.

clue.text: Uninhibited publicity material featuring single by pop group

indicators.note: the advertisement features, so holds within it, the other pieces

parts.note: an ad is publicity material
a band is a pop group
single means one

explanation.surface: A wild advert promotes a pop group's single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' looks like a record but means ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: abandoned behaviour is wild and free of restraint.

clue.text: Tory uncertainty brought about negative effect for sure

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the little uncertainty word is reversed

parts.note: an if is an uncertainty, as in 'no ifs or buts'
a dent is a setback or negative effect, as on savings

explanation.surface: A Conservative's doubts are said to have had a definite bad effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like 'caused', which would link the pieces; here it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: confident means certain, without doubt.

clue.text: Coaxes Jack and Bill to return with shouts of encouragement

indicators.note: to return means these two letters are read backwards

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
AC is short for account, a bill
ole is the cry of encouragement at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Jack and Bill are cheered and coaxed into coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns JAC round to CAJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cajole is to persuade by flattery.

clue.text: Wife taken in by a trace of local intonation

indicators.note: the wife is taken in by, so put inside, the trace

parts.note: a tang is a slight flavour or trace

explanation.surface: A wife falls for a man with a hint of regional accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive regional accent, a nasal quality of speech.

clue.text: Relevant to treatment of men with rage

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment on how to deal with angry men.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: germane means pertinent to the matter in hand.

clue.text: After an awkward situation May oddly gets lucky

parts.note: a jam is a tight spot

indicators.note: oddly means the first and third letters are taken

explanation.surface: After a tight spot, May strangely has good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammy is British slang for fortunate.

clue.text: Mao essentially ignored tea and coffee

indicators.note: the essence, the central letter, of the name is ignored

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Mao preferred tea and ignored coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a kind of fine coffee, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Almost certain to aim at the queen after king's capitulation

indicators.note: after places the aim and the queen after the king
almost means the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
R, from rex, is the abbreviation for king
an end is an aim, as in a means to an end
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Someone almost certain to target the queen after the king gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: SUR is 'almost' SURE; ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: surrender is the act of giving in to an enemy.

clue.text: Not sparkling yet

definitions.meaning: describes water or wine without bubbles
as an adverb, nevertheless or even so

explanation.definitionFit: Still water has no fizz; still also means nevertheless.

clue.text: Run without the right attitude at first

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, or without, as in ex-dividend

indicators.note: at first means the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone runs off lacking the right attitude from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is cricket: an extra is a run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, an extra is a run conceded by the fielding side, such as a wide or no-ball.

clue.text: Vital cure not exactly profitable

indicators.note: not exactly means the letters are not in their exact order

explanation.surface: A life-saving cure that is not quite a money-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lucrative means producing much money.

clue.text: Country in Africa principally associated with secret society

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society

indicators.note: principally means first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: An African country is chiefly linked to a secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Africa' tempts you to look there; Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Extremely stoical about lawyer facing jail for slander

indicators.note: the outer letters go about, around, the other pieces
extremely means the two extreme, outer letters are taken

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
DA is a district attorney, a US lawyer

explanation.surface: A stoical lawyer facing jail sues for slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandal can mean malicious gossip that harms a reputation.

clue.text: Tad lewd novel's pretentious writing

indicators.note: novel's is novel is: the letters are made new, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather risqué novel is dismissed as pompous prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is trivial or foolish talk or writing, nonsense.
